title: Hány órát dolgozol?: Duration with the Accusative

sections.title: Marking how long, not what
sections.content: You already know the accusative -t for direct objects, and you've seen it used for duration too, as in *nyolc órát alszom* ("I sleep eight hours"). The same pattern answers *Hány órát dolgozol?* ("How many hours do you work?") — put -t on the word for hours (*órát*; the number stays bare), even though nothing is technically being "acted on": *Nyolc órát dolgozom naponta.*

items.english: How many hours do you work per day?

items.spanish: Nyolc órát dolgozom, és délben egy óra szünetet tartok.
items.english: I work eight hours, and at noon I take a one-hour break.

items.spanish: Ma sok a túlóra, nagyon fárasztó ez a hét.
items.english: There's a lot of overtime today, this week is very tiring.

sections.content: *tart szünetet* ("takes a break") has its own accusative, because *szünet* is a real direct object — *egy óra szünetet tartok* ("I take an hour-long break"). Compare *Nyolc órát dolgozom*, where the hours themselves carry the -t.
